clue.text: Comrades Portia and Nerissa did in court

definitions.meaning: companions in games or friends

definitions.text: Portia and Nerissa did in court
definitions.meaning: in The Merchant of Venice the two women disguise themselves as men in the trial scene, so they played fellows

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare quiz question about two heroines' conduct at the trial.
explanation.walkthrough: Portia and Nerissa are the heroines of Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, who pose as a lawyer and his clerk.
explanation.definitionFit: Childhood companions or friends who share games are the same as comrades.

clue.text: Humour from North Riding taken the wrong way

indicators.note: taken the wrong way means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a jockey riding is said to be up

explanation.surface: Yorkshire wit misunderstood by outsiders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken the wrong way' reverses N plus UP. The North Riding was a division of Yorkshire, which the surface pretends to mean.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordplay on double meanings is a form of humour.

clue.text: Shoemaker's apparatus found in Roman villa

indicators.note: found in says the letters are inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Archaeologists unearthing a cobbler's equipment at a Roman villa.
explanation.walkthrough: The shoemaker is a farrier, who shoes horses on this iron block.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrier hammers horseshoes on an iron block, so it is a tool of a maker of shoes.

clue.text: Hurricane, perhaps, the source of heavy blows

definitions.meaning: the Hawker Hurricane was a Second World War warplane
a boxer, who throws heavy punches

explanation.surface: A storm described as the cause of strong winds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hurricane was a combat aircraft, and a boxer is a combatant who lands punches.

clue.text: Hearing organ, partly, in complicated passages

definitions.meaning: the inner ear, part of the organ of hearing
a maze of winding paths

explanation.surface: An anatomy lesson on the tangled channels of the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner ear's winding canals share their name with a maze of passages.

clue.text: Having advantage as solo flier?

definitions.meaning: being one step ahead of a rival
a lone person up in the air

explanation.surface: A lone pilot claims superiority.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a point ahead of an opponent means holding the advantage.

clue.text: Dreadful person that goes around cadging, ultimately

definitions.text: Dreadful person that goes around cadging, ultimately

indicators.note: goes around says the jumbled word surrounds the next letter
dreadful suggests the following word is mangled into a new order
ultimately points to the final letter of the word cadging

explanation.surface: An awful scrounger doing the rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' makes SPONER from PERSON, and 'goes around' puts it around G, the last letter of cadging. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrounger who lives off others by begging is a dreadful freeloader.

clue.text: Half hidden bend

indicators.note: only the front half of the word for hidden is kept here

parts.note: arcane means secret or hidden

explanation.surface: Something half out of sight around a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' takes the first three letters of ARCANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A curve or curved line is a bend.

clue.text: A bit of wind in the mountains

definitions.text: A bit of wind in the mountains

parts.words: A bit of wind in the mountains
parts.note: a wind instrument, the long wooden horn blown in the Alps

explanation.definitionFit: The long Swiss horn is a wind instrument played in the Alps.

clue.text: Light carrier for journey to Babylon?

definitions.text: Light carrier for journey to Babylon?

parts.words: Light carrier for journey to Babylon?
parts.note: the nursery rhyme asks if one can get to Babylon by candlelight, so what holds the light

explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'How many miles to Babylon?' answers that you can get there by candlelight.
explanation.definitionFit: A holder for a wax taper carries the light.

clue.text: Leaving in confusion without sailor being fit for sailing

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the jumble goes around the sailor
leaving in a muddle signals those letters are jumbled

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: Someone departs in a muddle, leaving the sailor behind, though the water is fine for sailing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: the anagram of LEAVING (NAVIGLE) goes around AB, making NAVIGABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Waters that ships can pass along are fit for sailing.

clue.text: Artist or writer

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A choice between painter and author.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir William Orpen was an Irish portrait painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpen was a twentieth-century portrait painter, so an example of a painter.

clue.text: Support for comfortable retirement

definitions.meaning: to prop up or reinforce
a long pillow placed on a bed, retiring meaning going to bed

explanation.surface: Advice about funding a pension.
explanation.definitionFit: To prop up something is to support it; the long pillow eases going to bed.

clue.text: Scene of conflict (not necessarily Hastings)

parts.note: a place where armies fought, the Battle of Hastings in 1066 being one example

explanation.definitionFit: Ground where armies clash is a scene of conflict, Hastings in 1066 being one.

clue.text: Like leaves making a drink in China

indicators.note: the drink is placed inside the word for china

parts.note: china is rhyming slang (china plate) for mate, a pal
gin is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: Tea leaves brewed into a drink in China.
explanation.walkthrough: China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, hence PAL; A and GIN go inside it, the capital C hiding the slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Paginal describes pages, the leaves of a book.

clue.text: House rose?

definitions.meaning: the English royal dynasty of Henry VII to Elizabeth I
the red and white heraldic rose badge of that dynasty

explanation.surface: Asking whether a home's value climbed.
explanation.definitionFit: The English royal dynasty founded by Henry VII adopted a combined rose as its badge.

clue.text: English desk /Americans sit on

definitions.meaning: in Britain, a small writing desk with a sloping top
in the US, a large sofa

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture used differently on each side of the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a small writing bureau in Britain and a couch in the US.

clue.text: Unusually safe in our base

indicators.note: unusually signals that these words appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Our base is remarkably safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a noun for a military base; here it is the adjective meaning wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Base in the sense of morally low means wicked or villainous.

clue.text: Extreme source of identification

parts.note: the very end of a digit, which leaves the prints that identify someone

explanation.definitionFit: The end of a finger is its extreme point and bears the print used to identify people.

clue.text: I haven't a pound change for book by Hobbes

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from libra

indicators.note: change signals that the letters are to be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A shopper short of change for a pound wanting to buy a philosophy book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' looks like coins but is the anagram signal for IHAVENTA plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hobbes's 1651 treatise on the state is titled after a biblical sea monster.

clue.text: Felicity gets odd pat on head

indicators.note: odd shows the word pat has its letters jumbled

parts.note: a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A woman named Felicity receives a strange pat on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' turns PAT into APT; 'Felicity' looks like a name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Felicity of expression means its suitability.

clue.text: Entertaining American serving edible plants

parts.note: something entertaining is fun
a GI is an American serviceman

explanation.surface: An amusing American waiter dishing up vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving' reads as waiting at table, but here an American serving in the forces is a GI.
explanation.definitionFit: Mushrooms are fungi, once classed as plants, many of them edible.

clue.text: Drunk advanced in time

definitions.meaning: very intoxicated
well on, late in the day

explanation.surface: Getting tipsy late in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone heavily intoxicated is well gone; a late hour is well advanced.

clue.text: Try to cool a movement out of control and extreme

parts.note: to fan someone is to try to cool them
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Someone flapping to cool down a protest movement that has got out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a movement out of control' suggests a political group; it is a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot holds extreme views, and as an adjective the word means excessively zealous.

clue.text: Musical group in paper reported

indicators.note: reported means the word is said aloud

parts.note: a quire is a measure of paper, 24 or 25 sheets

explanation.surface: A news story about a band in the local paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of singers is a musical group.

clue.text: Attention given to book set aside

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to give attention
Mark is a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: Someone paying attention to a book put to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve funds for a purpose is to set them aside.

clue.text: First lady's partner's President of United States

definitions.meaning: Eve, the first woman, had a partner, so belonging to him
John ... or John Quincy ...

explanation.surface: The husband of a First Lady is the American President.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve's mate in Genesis, possessive, and the surname of two US presidents.

clue.text: Secretly go and form union

definitions.meaning: run away in secret
marry, the purpose of running off

explanation.surface: Lovers who sneak away and get married.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers who run off together to wed without consent do so secretly.

clue.text: You know in your bones if his treatment works

definitions.text: You know in your bones if his treatment works

parts.words: You know in your bones if his treatment works
parts.note: a practitioner who manipulates bones and joints, so success is felt in the skeleton

explanation.definitionFit: A manipulative therapist treats the skeleton and joints, so his work is felt in one's bones.

clue.text: Objective of Haggard's heroine

parts.note: H. Rider Haggard's novel She; the objective case of that pronoun

explanation.definitionFit: The accusative form of the feminine pronoun is the grammatical object form.

clue.text: Morse's unit I must have in the other case

definitions.text: Morse's unit I must have in the other case

parts.words: Morse's unit I must have in the other case
parts.note: the short signal of Morse code, whose other name, dit, has an I where this word has an O

explanation.definitionFit: The short signal in Morse code is also called a dit, spelt with an I instead.

clue.text: She barely finishes her turn

parts.note: a performer who ends her act with hardly any clothes on

explanation.definitionFit: A burlesque performer undresses during her act, ending it nearly naked.
